description: Persistent single-launch megakernel for the n=512 B=640 cluster using thread-block clusters + distributed shared memory. One cluster of 2-4 CTAs cooperatively factors each 512x512 matrix with the panel shared via DSMEM/TMA multicast, tcgen05 tensor-core trailing updates (10.0a PTX), warp specialization (producer warps load/convert, consumer warps MMA). Grid-stride persistent over the 640 matrices so the whole cluster shape launches once. Emit (H,tau) compact. Attack launch overhead AND occupancy together.

Trial 1: FP32 persistent single-launch megakernel for n=512. One CTA/matrix, grid-stride persistent over batch (148 CTAs, one wave + restride), blocked Householder nb=32, panel factored unblocked in SMEM, compact-WY trailing update as in-CTA FP32 GEMM. geqrf-exact (H,tau); off-grid n->geqrf. All test shapes + all 3 guards CLEAN. n=512 cluster ~1.07M->~110k us each (~9.7x); geomean 133434->61474 us (2.17x). No tensor cores yet; trailing GEMM is FP32 SIMT.

Trial 2: TF32 WMMA (mma.sync sm_100a) trailing update, 3xTF32 hi/lo split for ~FP32 accuracy, FP32 accumulate, 512 threads. Removed FP16 buffers (TF32 reads FP32 SMEM). All n=512 cases + 3 guards CLEAN. n=512 cluster ~110k->~50.5k us each (2.2x over FP32 SIMT trial 1); geomean 61474->47433 us (2.81x vs baseline). 3-pass GEMM is the accuracy-safe version; 1xTF32 (NPASS=1) is 3x cheaper but coordinator reports it fails ill-cond cases on HW - will test next.

Trial 3: 2xTF32 trailing update (ah*bh+ah*bl). Passes all n=512 incl band/rowscale with margin (1xTF32 fails band 20.1 on HW; 2x halves residual). geomean 47358 ~ identical to 3xTF32 47433 -> KEY FINDING: trailing GEMM is NOT the bottleneck; cutting GEMM passes 3->2 barely moved it. Megakernel is occupancy/latency bound (trial-1 ncu: 1.99 active warps/sched, 45% SMEM-scoreboard stalls, 1 CTA/SM due to ~148KB SMEM). Next: profile to confirm, then attack occupancy (clusters/more CTAs/SM) and serial panel factorization.

Trial 4: NB=16 (SMEM 148KB->81KB, occupancy 25%->50%, 2 CTAs/SM). geomean 47358->46264 (cluster 50.2k->46.8k each). Small win: doubling occupancy is offset by 2x more serial panels. Confirms the barrier-heavy serial panel factorization is the real bottleneck (trial-3 ncu: 36% stalls 'waiting for sibling warps at CTA barrier', 22% compute). Need to attack the serial panel: warp-specialize or cluster (2-4 CTAs/matrix sharing panel via DSMEM) so the trailing GEMM has more parallelism per matrix.

Trial 5: step-1 W=V^T C reads C directly from global memory via WMMA (no SMEM staging, no per-K-strip barrier); each warp owns output tiles grid-strided, loops K independently. Removed the dominant idle-warp + barrier source. Cluster 46.8k->35.3k each; geomean 46264->42123 (3.17x vs baseline). Next: profile new bottleneck; step-3 and panel factorization remain.

Trial 6: launch grid=2*SMs (296) so 2 CTAs/SM resident (occupancy 25%->50%). The persistent grid was exactly 148=#SMs, leaving the 2-CTA/SM SMEM headroom (81KB/CTA) unused. Grid-stride handles batch. Cluster 35.3k->24.3k each; geomean 42123->37182 (3.59x vs baseline). All guards CLEAN. Sibling cuBLAS at 16.8k. Next: try 3 CTAs/SM (need smaller SMEM), reduce panel-factorization SMEM-scoreboard stalls (33.7%), per-matrix 1xTF32 fast path, or clusters.

Trial 7: step-3 stores result straight to global C via WMMA accumulator preload (load C->acc, acc+=V*(-W) with W negated in step 2, store->C). Removed 16KB Sout staging + subtract loop -> SMEM 81KB->65KB -> 3 CTAs/SM (grid=444). Cluster 24.3k->20.1k each; geomean 37182->34881 (3.82x baseline). All guards CLEAN. Sibling 16.8k. Next: re-profile; attack panel-factorization SMEM-scoreboard stalls and/or 4 CTAs/SM, per-matrix 1xTF32 fast path.

Trial 8: __launch_bounds__(512,3) caps registers (was 64/thread, register-limited to 2 CTAs/SM) to enable 3 CTAs/SM. Marginal: geomean 34881->34753. Confirms occupancy is no longer binding; panel-factorization barriers (33% stalls) dominate now. Next: restructure panel factorization to cut __syncthreads count.

Trial 9: parallelize within-panel reflector apply. All dots for reflector c computed in parallel (one warp/target column, warp-shfl reduction, no block sync), one sync, fused axpy over (cp,r), one sync -> ~3*(nbc-c) barriers/column collapsed to 2. Cluster 19.9k->17.8k each; geomean 34753->33519 (3.98x baseline). Approaching sibling 16.8k. All guards CLEAN. Next: parallelize the norm reduction / column writeback syncs too, or cluster/DSMEM.

Trial 10: defer panel writeback to a single pass after the column loop (save betas in SMEM). Neutral (geomean 33518, cluster 17.8k) -- writeback syncs were not critical-path. Remaining panel cost is the serial norm reductions + inherent column dependency, not writeback. Note: for B=640>>148 SMs the GPU is already saturated with independent matrices at 3 CTAs/SM, so thread-block CLUSTERS add no tensor throughput here (clusters fit the large-n few-matrix shapes, not n=512 B=640). Next: trailing-GEMM efficiency / NB tuning / per-matrix 1xTF32.

Trial 11: step-3 register tiling (NCOL=4, reuse V fragment across N-tiles). REGRESSION cluster 17.8k->21.3k (geomean 35572). K=NB=16 too small for A-reuse benefit; extra accumulators/fragments raise register pressure -> fewer CTAs/SM. Confirms step 3 not the bottleneck and occupancy is register-sensitive. Reverting step 3 to the simple per-tile version (trial 10, 33518) for next trials.

Trial 12: single-warp (warp-shuffle) reflector formation, no block reductions in the panel; reverted trial-11 step-3 regression. Neutral (geomean 33597, cluster 17.9k). KEY: panel barrier reductions (trials 10,12) are neutral -> at 3 CTAs/SM the serial panel is hidden by sibling CTAs; kernel is THROUGHPUT-bound (38% compute), not panel-latency-bound. Levers left: reduce trailing-GEMM work (per-matrix 1xTF32 routing for well-cond), better GEMM tiling without register pressure, or accept ~parity with sibling cuBLAS (16.8k).

Trial 13: form compact-WY T via a Gram matrix G=V^T V computed with ONE WMMA GEMM (3xTF32) instead of O(NB^2)=~256 serial block reductions/panel (a hidden sync storm). T formed column-wise from G. The T-formation reductions were a MAJOR bottleneck. Cluster 17.9k->15.5k each; geomean 33597->31988 (4.17x baseline), now beating sibling cuBLAS 16.8k. 3xTF32 Gram needed (2xTF32 Gram flagged a mixed diff-guard variant at 21); trailing stays 2xTF32. All guards CLEAN. Earlier finding: per-matrix 1x/2x routing NOT viable (band has 1xTF32 resid 1023 yet benign magnitude stats -> unclassifiable). Next: profile; further sync reduction in panel apply, or accept floor.

Trial 14: drop redundant SMEM fragment reloads (derive al/bl lo-parts from loaded hi fragments). Marginal (geomean 31925). PROFILE SHIFT: after removing the T-formation sync storm (trial 13), the kernel is now SMEM-BANDWIDTH bound (61% mem throughput, 1.16 TB/s, 39% wait-on-SMEM stalls), DRAM only 15%. SMEM traffic = WMMA fragment loads of Vp/Wm. To cut it needs fragment reuse (register tiling) but that costs occupancy (trial 11 regressed). Next: gentle register tiling (NCOL=2), or accept ~15.4k cluster (beats sibling 16.8k).

Trial 15: step-1 register-tiling sweep to cut SMEM-load traffic (reuse V fragment across NCOL n-tiles). NCOL=4->33679, NCOL=2->32019, both worse than simple 1-tile/warp (31925) -- register pressure cuts occupancy more than SMEM savings. Reverted to simple step 1 (geomean 31968, cluster 15.4k). Register tiling unfavorable at this CTA size (confirms trial 11). SMEM-bandwidth bound but can't cheaply reduce it without losing occupancy. Cluster 15.4k beats sibling cuBLAS 16.8k. Diminishing returns on n=512; openings: per-shape NB/threads, or extend the megakernel to n=1024 (other briefs' territory, big geomean lever).

Trial 16: pad SMEM leading dims ldv=ldw=N+8 to break WMMA fragment-load bank conflicts (N=512 = multiple of 32 banks serialized the tile loads; SMEM bandwidth was binding at 61%). BIG WIN: cluster 15.4k->12.6k each; geomean 31968->29846 (4.47x baseline), far below sibling cuBLAS 16.8k. All guards CLEAN. Next: re-profile (new bottleneck?), tune pad amount, revisit precision now that SMEM pressure is lower.

Trial 17: factor IN PLACE (write QR over the input buffer, skip the A->H copy) to save 1MB/matrix global copy. PASSED validation (test mode calls once) but FAILED benchmark (scaled resid 3e4): eval.py benchmark REUSES the same input object across timed repeats, so the 2nd repeat factors an already-factored matrix. In-place is unsafe -> reverted to the fresh-output A->H copy (trial 16). Lesson: the A->H copy is correctness-required under input reuse.

Trial 18: revert in-place (trial 17) to fresh-output A->H copy; recovered best state. geomean 29836 (cluster ~12.55k each), all guards CLEAN. This is the current best: single-launch persistent megakernel, 1 CTA/matrix, NB=16 blocked Householder, warp-shuffle reflector formation, Gram-matrix(3xTF32 WMMA) compact-WY T, 2xTF32 WMMA trailing update, SMEM bank-conflict padding (ldv=N+8), 3 CTAs/SM. 4.47x vs baseline 133434; n=512 cluster ~1.07M->12.55k (85x); beats sibling cuBLAS 16.8k by 25%.

Trial 19: strip-mine trailing update (STRIP=256 cols) -> W buffer NB x STRIP (16.5KB) not NB x tcols. Steps 1-3 independent per column so exact. Cluster 12.55k->11.88k each; geomean 29836->29282 (4.55x baseline). STRIP=128+launch_bounds(4) regressed (strip-sync overhead + register spill); STRIP=256+launch_bounds(3) wins. All guards CLEAN. Registers (40/thread) cap occupancy at 3 CTAs/SM even though SMEM now allows more. Sweep STRIP further?

n=512 megakernel worked hard across 19 trials: geomean 133434->29331 us (4.55x), n=512 cluster ~1.07M->~11.9k us each (~89x), BEATS sibling cuBLAS 16.8k by ~30%. BEST commit 00fa8e34. Single-launch persistent megakernel: 1 CTA/512x512 matrix, grid-stride over batch, NB=16 blocked Householder. Wins (biggest first): SMEM bank-conflict padding ldv=N+8 (15.4k->12.6k); Gram-matrix WMMA for compact-WY T replacing O(NB^2) block-reduction sync-storm (17.9k->15.5k); 2 then 3 CTAs/SM via launch_bounds(512,3)+small SMEM (35k->20k); 2xTF32 WMMA trailing update (110k->50k); strip-mine trailing cols STRIP=256 (12.55k->11.9k); direct-global-C step1 GEMM no SMEM staging; parallel warp-per-column panel apply; step3 stores via acc-preload (no staging). NEGATIVE/rejected: register tiling (steps 1&3, any NCOL) regresses - register pressure cuts occupancy; 1xTF32 FAILS band (resid 1023, undetectable by cheap stats so per-matrix routing infeasible); BF16 fails rowscale/mixed; NB=32 too much SMEM (1 CTA/SM); 4 CTAs/SM spills (regress); in-place factoring corrupts under harness input-reuse; panel barrier reductions neutral (hidden by occupancy). State: SMEM-bandwidth + barrier co-bound (50/39% mem/compute, 60% occ, regs cap at 3 CTAs/SM). BIGGEST OPEN LEVER (off my brief): the geomean is now dominated by the 3 n=1024 shapes at 239k each (still baseline geqrf); this megakernel is parameterized by N and should route n=1024 directly for a huge geomean drop - overlaps brief-1/brief-4 so left for the manager to assign. Other openings: fuse Gram into step1 to drop a barrier+V-reload; reduce kernel registers to unlock 4 CTAs/SM without spilling; per-shape NB/threads; tcgen05/cluster path remains unbuilt (clusters add no throughput at B=640>>148 SMs but would help the large-n few-matrix shapes).

Trial 20: extend megakernel to n=1024 (add 1024 to _SUPPORTED). SAME kernel/structure (only caches NB-panel+tiles in SMEM, streams trailing from global) so n=1024 just works. PER-SHAPE: n=512 cluster (3,7,9,10) ~11.93/11.96/11.94/11.94k us; n=1024 (4,8,11) 22.52/22.57/22.56k us (was ~239k each, ~10.6x - work-starved at B=60 under serial cuSOLVER). geomean 29331->16251 (8.2x baseline). Trial 21: route n=176,352 to megakernel (n=2048/4096 stay geqrf). PER-SHAPE: n=176 22.1k->539us (41x), n=352 50.5k->1747us (29x), n=512 cluster ~11.9k, n=1024 ~22.5k, n=2048 77k(geqrf), n=4096 52.3k(geqrf), n=32 324(geqrf). geomean 16251->9001 (14.8x baseline). n=2048 on megakernel REGRESSED to 124.7k (work-starved B=8 vs 148 SMs); n=4096 panel>SMEM. All guards CLEAN. Sibling global best 6407. Gap now from n=2048/4096 (geqrf) + n=1024 (22.5k). Next: optimize n=1024 occupancy, then attack n=2048/4096 (needs multi-CTA-per-matrix / cluster split since work-starved).

Trial 22: cooperative multi-CTA-per-matrix kernel (grid.sync, redundant panel, column-sliced trailing) for work-starved n>=1024. G CTAs cooperatively factor one matrix; G from occupancy (G=4 for n=1024 B=60). n=1024 ~22.5k->~14.7k each (1.53x); geomean 9001->8098 (16.5x baseline). All guards CLEAN. PER-SHAPE now: n=176 539, n=352 1747, n=512 ~11.9k, n=1024 ~14.7k, n=2048 77k(geqrf), n=4096 52.3k(geqrf), n=32 324. Sibling 6407. Gap from n=2048/4096 (geqrf) + n=512(11.9k). Next: route n=2048 to coop kernel (G=8, was work-starved on 1-CTA); push n=512.

Trial 23: route n=2048 to cooperative kernel (G=8). n=2048 77k(geqrf)->38.3k (2x); was 124k on single-CTA (work-starved). geomean 8098->7657 (17.4x baseline). PER-SHAPE: n=176 539, n=352 1747, n=512 ~11.9k, n=1024 ~14.7k, n=2048 38.3k, n=4096 52.1k(geqrf), n=32 324. All guards CLEAN. Sibling 6407. Remaining gap: n=4096 (52.1k geqrf, panel>SMEM needs NB=8 or row-tiling), n=512 (11.9k), n=2048 (38.3k could improve with bigger G/tcgen05). Next: n=4096 via NB=8 coop, push n=512/2048.

Trial 24: cooperative G cap 8->16. n=2048 38.3k->38.1k (marginal), n=1024 unchanged. geomean 7657->7613 (17.5x). Diminishing returns: redundant panel (G CTAs each factor full panel) grows with G. DSMEM (factor panel once, share across cluster) would remove redundancy. All guards CLEAN. Next: profile coop kernel for redundant-panel cost; n=4096 via NB=8.

Extended megakernel to large N (priority 1) + built the brief's multi-CTA cluster path. geomean 29331->7636 us (overall 133434->7636 = 17.5x); BEST commit 179882059. Two kernels: (1) single-CTA-per-matrix megakernel for n in {176,352,512} (batch>=SMs); (2) cooperative multi-CTA-per-matrix megakernel (grid.sync, G CTAs cooperatively factor one matrix, redundant panel + disjoint trailing-column slices, grid.sync between panels) for work-starved n in {1024,2048}. PER-SHAPE us (for COMBINE decision): n=32 B=20 324(geqrf), n=176 B=40 541(mega, was 22.1k=41x), n=352 B=40 1754(mega, was 50.5k=29x), n=512 B=640 ~11.9k each x4 (was ~1.07M=89x), n=1024 B=60 ~14.7k each x3 (coop G=4, was 239k=16x; single-CTA gave 22.5k), n=2048 B=8 38.2k (coop G=16, beats geqrf 77k=2x; single-CTA 124k work-starved), n=4096 B=2 52.1k(geqrf). My megakernel WINS n=176/352/512/1024/2048; n=4096 stays geqrf (panel 4096x16=256KB > 227KB SMEM, and NB can't drop below 16 for the 16x16 WMMA tiles) -- the sibling's cuBLAS likely wins n=4096, so a per-shape COMBINE (my path for n<=2048, sibling/geqrf for n=4096) should beat both. Validation+all 3 guards CLEAN at every committed trial. NOTE: cooperative kernels can't be profiled (grid.sync deadlocks ncu/nsys), so coop tuning was benchmark-driven. OPEN LEVERS: true thread-block clusters + DSMEM/TMA-multicast to factor the panel ONCE per cluster instead of redundantly (est ~6-12% on n=1024/2048; the brief's literal ask, not yet built -- I used cooperative-groups grid.sync for the multi-CTA parallelism instead); fuse Gram into step-1 GEMM (drop a barrier + V reload); n=4096 needs a panel-height-tiled (TSQR-style) factorization to fit SMEM; tcgen05 MMA unbuilt. Sibling global best 6407 -- my 7636 is within 1.19x using a fundamentally different single-launch fused-megakernel approach that should combine well.

Trial 25: grid.sync -> thread-block cluster.sync (true clusters, cudaLaunchKernelEx + cluster dim, sm_100a). REGRESSION: n=1024 14.7k->46.3k, n=2048 38k->155k (geomean 7613->18406). ncu NOW WORKS on the coop path (cluster.sync doesn't deadlock ncu): 54% of stall cycles at the cluster.sync barrier (vs ~32% grid.sync). cluster.sync across G SMs (G=5 n=1024, G=16 n=2048) wave-scheduled is MORE expensive than grid.sync on a fully-resident persistent grid. Correct (all guards CLEAN). Next: try small G (cheaper cluster barrier) + DSMEM (factor panel once) to see if clusters can match grid.sync; else revert to grid.sync (trial 24).

Trial 26: cluster + DSMEM (rank 0 factors panel+Gram+T once, shares via cluster.map_shared_rank -> local SMEM copy). MEASURED negative: DSMEM not faster than redundant-panel (redundant factorization is already free/parallel; DSMEM adds copy+sync). Larger G needed for n=2048 makes cluster.sync prohibitive: n=1024 G=5 22.9k, n=2048 G=16 87.9k (geomean 9139). CONCLUSION: cluster.sync cost scales with G; work-starved large-N needs large G; so true clusters (cluster.sync) LOSE to grid.sync (trial 24=7613) for this kernel. ncu confirmed cluster.sync = 54% of stall cycles. Reverting to grid.sync best. Brief's literal cluster+DSMEM ask thoroughly built+measured.

Trial 27: revert to grid.sync multi-CTA (=trial 24 best, geomean 7635). The brief's literal cluster.sync+DSMEM ask was fully built (trials 25,26) and MEASURED to regress (18406, 9139) -- cluster.sync cost scales with G; work-starved n=2048 needs large G; grid.sync on a resident persistent grid is cheaper. PER-SHAPE (final): n=1024 14.76k (grid.sync G=4-ish), n=2048 38.2k. Sibling: n=2048 ~21k -- they still beat me on n=2048 (their cuBLAS spreads one matrix across SMs better than my fused per-matrix kernel for B=8). I WIN n=176/352/512/1024; LOSE n=2048/4096. Combine: my path n<=1024, sibling n>=2048.

Built the brief's literal cluster+DSMEM ask and MEASURED it. BEST commit 94789bd9 (grid.sync multi-CTA), geomean 7638 us (17.5x vs baseline 133434). DID per coordinator priority-1: (trial 25) converted cooperative grid.sync -> TRUE thread-block clusters (cudaLaunchKernelEx + cluster dim, cluster.sync, sm_100a); (trial 26) added DSMEM -- rank 0 factors the panel+Gram+T ONCE, other ranks read via cluster.map_shared_rank into local SMEM (WMMA can't read DSMEM directly). RESULT: both REGRESS vs grid.sync. cluster.sync n=1024 46.3k/n=2048 155k (G auto); +DSMEM n=1024 22.9k/n=2048 87.9k. ncu NOW WORKS on the coop path (cluster.sync, unlike grid.sync, does not deadlock ncu) and shows cluster.sync = 54% of stall cycles. ROOT CAUSE: cluster.sync cost scales with cluster size G (cross-SM barrier over G SMs, called once per panel x ~N/16 panels); work-starved large-N (n=2048 B=8) needs LARGE G for SM-fill parallelism, but large-G cluster.sync is prohibitive; grid.sync on a fully-resident persistent grid is the cheaper barrier here. DSMEM does NOT help because the redundant panel factorization it removes was already free (each rank on its own SM, parallel) -- DSMEM only adds a copy+sync. Reverted to grid.sync best (trial 24=27). PER-SHAPE us (FINAL, for COMBINE): n=32 324(geqrf), n=176 541(mega), n=352 1754(mega), n=512 ~11.9k x4 (mega 1-CTA), n=1024 ~14.7k x3 (grid.sync multi-CTA G~4), n=2048 38.3k (grid.sync multi-CTA G~16), n=4096 52.1k(geqrf). HONEST COMPARISON vs sibling: I WIN n=176/352/512/1024; sibling beats me on n=2048 (~21k vs my 38k) and presumably n=4096 -- their separate-panel-kernel+cuBLAS spreads ONE matrix's trailing GEMM across all SMs per panel, which a single fused launch can't match for few matrices (B=8,2). My fused megakernel's edge is n<=1024 (batch>=SMs, single launch avoids the per-panel launch storm). COMBINE: route my megakernel for n<=1024, sibling/cuBLAS for n>=2048. All guards CLEAN at every committed trial. Open (low-yield): a cheaper inter-CTA sync than grid.sync/cluster.sync would unlock large-G multi-CTA, but sm_100a offers none beyond these; tcgen05 MMA unbuilt (would speed the trailing GEMM but not the barrier-bound large-N).

Trial 28: FP8(e4m3)/NVFP4 trailing-update numerics, tested via faithful prototypes running the REAL check_implementation gate (torch.float8_e4m3fn casts, FP32 accumulate, exact blocked-QR algorithm). MEASURED NEGATIVE across all variants at the LOOSEST gate (n=1024 dense, gate scaled<=20): 1-term FP8 fails (single GEMM rel err 3.75e-2 = ~15x the 2.4e-3 n=1024 budget); 2/3/4-term hi/lo FP8 fail (4-term=63.6, and 4-term costs the SAME as the working 2xTF32 which gives 0.69); per-row-scaled 1xFP8 fails; FP8-step1-only and FP8-step3-only both fail. ROOT CAUSE: e4m3's 3-bit mantissa => ~3.75% per-GEMM relative error, the QR factor residual compounds it over ~64-128 panels; block-scaling fixes range not mantissa; NVFP4 (e2m1, 1 mantissa bit) is strictly worse. The fused-cast-during-staging advantage is real+free in the megakernel but cannot overcome the mantissa floor. classify-on-convert (part 2) is moot: FP8 fails the WELL-CONDITIONED class too, not just band/rowscale. HEAD unchanged at best grid.sync 7638 (trial 27). Untested execution path: a raw-PTX mma.sync.m16n8k32.e4m3 LIVE kernel (nvcuda::wmma has no FP8 fragments in CUDA13) -- would only confirm this correctness verdict for a kernel that cannot pass validation, so not built. PER-SHAPE best unchanged: n=512 ~11.9k, n=1024 ~14.7k, n=2048 38.3k.

FP8/NVFP4-in-megakernel bet: tested rigorously, MEASURED NEGATIVE. BEST commit 94789bd9 unchanged (grid.sync multi-CTA megakernel, geomean 7638 us, 17.5x baseline; n=512 ~11.9k, n=1024 ~14.7k, n=2048 38.3k; all guards CLEAN). Did per operator request: prototyped FP8(e4m3) + NVFP4 trailing updates as faithful prototypes running the EXACT check_implementation correctness gate (torch.float8_e4m3fn casts, FP32 accumulate, identical blocked-QR algorithm to the live kernel). VERDICT at the LOOSEST gate (n=1024 dense, scaled<=20): EVERY FP8 variant FAILS -- 1-term (single-GEMM rel err 3.75e-2 ~ 15x the 2.4e-3 budget), 2/3/4-term hi/lo (4-term=63.6 and costs SAME as the working 2xTF32=0.69), per-row-scaled 1xFP8, FP8-step1-only, FP8-step3-only. ROOT CAUSE: e4m3's 3-bit mantissa = ~3.75% per-GEMM relative error; the QR factor residual compounds it over ~64-128 panels; block-scaling (NVFP4 microscaling) fixes exponent RANGE not MANTISSA, and NVFP4's 1 mantissa bit is strictly worse than e4m3. The coordinator's fused-cast-during-staging insight is CORRECT and free in the megakernel, but it cannot overcome the FP-low mantissa floor vs the QR factor gate. classify-on-convert (the 2-stat per-row-dynamic-range + density classifier) is MOOT here because FP8 fails the WELL-CONDITIONED majority too, not only band/rowscale -- there is no class for which FP8 is both fast and gate-accurate. The only speed-positive variant (1-term FP8 @ 2x TF32 throughput) misses by 15x; the only gate-accuracy-approaching variant (4-term) costs the same as 2xTF32 and still fails. NOT BUILT: a raw-PTX mma.sync.m16n8k32.e4m3 LIVE kernel (nvcuda::wmma exposes no FP8 fragments in CUDA13, so live FP8 needs hand-written PTX) -- it would only reproduce this checker verdict for a kernel that cannot pass validation (so never scorable/mergeable), at high cost on a contended fleet; the faithful prototype already runs the real gate. OPEN (for the manager): 2xTF32 remains the precision floor that passes; if a future format with >=8 mantissa bits at >TF32 throughput existed it would help, but FP8/FP4 do not. Combine guidance stands: my megakernel wins n<=1024 per-shape (single-launch, no per-panel launch storm), sibling cuBLAS wins n>=2048.
